cover.headline_html: 3 myths that block your federal entry.

myths.label: The Past-Performance Block
myths.myth_text: You need past federal performance before GSA will approve you.
myths.reality_text: GSA Schedule eligibility requires 2 years in business and $25K in revenue — not federal experience. Confusing eligibility with winning task orders is what keeps most businesses from ever applying.

myths.label: The Guarantee Assumption
myths.myth_text: Getting on Schedule means agencies will start calling you.
myths.reality_text: The Schedule removes procurement friction — it doesn't generate demand. You still need to market, respond to RFQs, and build agency relationships. The Schedule opens the door; you still have to walk through it.

myths.label: The Timeline Trap
myths.myth_text: The GSA application takes a few weeks if you're organized.
myths.reality_text: Typical GSA Schedule approval: 6–12 months from submission to award. Pricing audits, compliance review, CO negotiations, clarification rounds. Plan for it — or get caught by it.

close.close_question: Drop the assumption you held longest about federal contracting — and what changed your mind.
